subject: Updated subprocessor notification — clarification for EU DPO review
messages:
From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@eurcorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-20T09:14:00Z
Subject: Request: updated subprocessors + transfer mechanisms

Hi Jonas,

EurCorp's privacy team is doing a routine check ahead of a renewal and we noticed a recent line in your notifications about "updates to subprocessors in Q4". Can you send over the latest subprocessor list and clarify which data transfer mechanisms apply for EU customer data (SCCs, adequacy, or other)?

A few specific asks from our DPO:
- Full list of subprocessors (names, locations, purpose)
- Whether any new subprocessors will have access to customer content in plaintext
- Confirmation of SCCs or equivalent for any transfers outside the EEA
- Whether customer-managed KMS is available for our tenancy

We are working to complete our sign-off by the first week of December, so a response by Nov 26 would be ideal.

Thanks,
Elena Novak
Data Protection Officer
EurCorp

Attachment: eurcorp_review_checklist.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@eurcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-21T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: updated subprocessors + transfer mechanisms

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the checklist. Looping in Marissa from Legal/Contracts to help with the SCCs and KMS details.

Short answers up front:
- We'll attach the current subprocessor inventory (see subprocessors_list_v2 and note in-line below about an upcoming vendor change planned 2025-12-01).
- New vendor (CloudEdge Analytics) will be engaged for telemetry/observability processing. They will process telemetry and aggregated logs only; they will not have access to customer prompt/response content in plaintext.
- We rely on SCCs for EEA -> non-EEA transfers; where a subprocessors' processing occurs inside the EEA, SCCs are not necessary but are still documented.
- Customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted customers we offer a partner-managed KM option. If you require customer-managed keys for your account, we'll note it for the DPA amendment path.

I'm attaching the subprocessor inventory PDF and a short SCCs summary. Marissa — can you confirm the legal text we would propose to update in the DPA to cover the CloudEdge addition and the KMS wording?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: subprocessors_list_v2.pdf (attachment stub), SCCs_onepager.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@eurcorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: EurCorp Data Privacy Team <dpo@eurcorp.com>
Date: 2025-11-25T08:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: updated subprocessors + transfer mechanisms

Jonas / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying Qs from our technical reviewers and legal: 

1) CloudEdge Analytics — where in the EU will their processing take place? We need country-level data for our records (we prefer Ireland/DE/FR but need the exact site).
2) "Telemetry and aggregated logs" — can you confirm that this excludes any customer-generated model inputs/outputs? Are there any scenarios where CloudEdge would see full-text prompts/responses?
3) For the hosted offering: is the KMS partner able to provide Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) or is it solely Redwood-managed? If BYOK is not available, please note that as a conditional requirement in our DPA redline.

We have an internal deadline of Dec 4 to accept any subprocessor changes prior to contract renewal. If you anticipate the CloudEdge onboarding on Dec 1 as mentioned, please provide the definitive list and a short security summary (ISO27001, encryption at rest/in-transit, access controls) by Dec 2.

Best,
Elena Novak
DPO, EurCorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@eurcorp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-03T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: updated subprocessors + transfer mechanisms

Elena — apologies for the longer thread, and thanks for the precise questions. I'm Marissa from Legal (copied Evelyn from Security/Trust for technical confirmation). Below are consolidated responses and the attachments you requested.

1) CloudEdge Analytics — processing location
- Confirmed: primary processing for telemetry will occur in Frankfurt, DE (AWS eu-central-1). They also have a secondary support site in Dublin, IE but no production processing outside EU for your data.

2) Access to customer content
- CloudEdge will receive only telemetry, usage metrics and anonymized/aggregated logs. They will not have access to customer prompt/response content (plaintext) under our configuration. We restrict log retention and employ redaction rules on any logs that might contain PII or content-like payloads. Evelyn: see comment below for technical controls.

3) KMS / BYOK
- Hosted customers: partner-managed BYOK is available via our key management partner (we can enable tenant-scoped keys). It's not currently self-service in the hosted UI; activation requires an order and short onboarding (we can surface that in the DPA amendment). For Dedicated/Private deployments BYOK is supported and fully customer-controlled.

4) SCCs and legal mechanism
- SCCs are in place for any subprocessors performing processing outside of the EEA. For CloudEdge (Frankfurt) no SCCs are required but their processing is documented in the subprocessor appendix and covered by our DPA amendment. Attached is an SCCs_summary.docx and the updated subprocessors list (v3) that includes CloudEdge and the technical summary.

5) Security posture
- CloudEdge: ISO 27001 certified, TLS1.2+ for in-transit, AES-256 at rest, role-based access controls with short-term credentials, quarterly attestations to Redwood Security team.

Next steps:
- We've prepared a short DPA amendment that adds CloudEdge to the subprocessor appendix and includes the BYOK activation flow for hosted customers. If you want, we can raise a DocuSign amendment and target signature by Dec 10.
- If EurCorp requires any additional contractual guarantees (e.g., encryption default to tenant key, more restrictive retention), flag them and we can provide a tailored redline.

Attachments: subprocessors_list_v3.pdf, SCCs_summary.docx

Best regards,

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
